story.head: Where the Predators have the edge: the penalty kill
paras: The Red Wings have won two in a row, while the Predators (13-6-6) lost 6-5 in a shootout to Utah last night. Going in, the Predators are third in the Central (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Red Wings seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 25th).

The Predators’ record (.640) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.526), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. The Red Wings have played better than their record (.460) says: their chances are worth about .527, and their finishing has held them back. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest), get pinned in their own end on long shifts (30th) and give up a lot of shots (30th). As for the Red Wings, they leave the shooting to their forwards (4th lowest) and ice the puck a lot (29th). They also block more shots than almost anyone (3rd), so the Wings are likely to get in the way of a lot of the Predators’ shots. Detroit has scored 2.60 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. The Predators have the edge over the Red Wings on the penalty kill.

Filip Forsberg (10 G / 17 A / 27 P in 25 GP) leads the Predators in scoring, with four goals in six games against Detroit since 2023-24. Steven Stamkos (12 G / 12 A / 24 P in 25 GP) has a team-high twelve goals. For the Red Wings, Lucas Raymond (10 G / 14 A / 24 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Viktor Arvidsson (9 G / 9 A / 18 P in 25 GP) is next in line.
Justus Annunen (4-2-0 / .863 SV% in 6 GS) has struggled for Nashville so far, but will likely start. Daniil Tarasov (4-4-2 / .930 SV% in 9 GS) has been terrific for Detroit and will likely start.
